common.tagline: Many photographs of the same sky, one deeper image

home.title: An astrophotography repository that combines many people's frames
home.subtitle: Upload your exposures with full metadata, choose their licence, and let them join other observers' frames to produce deeper, better-sampled images with verifiable provenance.

gains.title: What you gain by combining many photographs
gains.p1: When many people photograph the same object from different places and at different times, adding their frames buys four measurable things. Depth: noise falls as the square root of the accumulated exposure, so an object no single frame detects shows up with hundreds of contributions. Sampling: observers never point in exactly the same way, and that free sub-pixel diversity recovers detail that each individual pixel grid aliases away; on wide-field, badly undersampled setups there is a genuine factor of 1.5 to 3 in effective linear sampling to reclaim. Dynamic range: different exposures give unsaturated cores and deep outskirts at the same time. And the time domain: a decade of contributions is a time series — variable stars, asteroids, proper motions — and it is by far the most scientifically valuable output.
gains.p2: What you do not gain is angular resolution through aperture synthesis. Two people a thousand kilometres apart photographing Andromeda do not form a thousand-kilometre telescope: a camera records intensity, not the electric field, and phase is destroyed irrecoverably at the moment of detection. Combining images adds intensities, which improves statistics; it does not add fields, which is what would improve resolution. This is not a software limitation and more photographs will not fix it. The ceiling remains the diffraction limit of the best contributing optic; deconvolution can sharpen inside the optical passband by a modest, prior-dependent factor, and whenever that happens we label it. There is no Event Horizon Telescope for amateurs here, and saying so is part of the product.

limits.title: What we will never promise
limits.aperture: Event Horizon Telescope-style resolution gains from combining separated observers. Incoherent intensity addition does not synthesize an aperture.
limits.diffraction: Resolving below the diffraction limit of the best contributing optic, except by modest, prior-dependent deconvolution, which is always labelled.
limits.parallax: Parallax or 3D depth for anything outside the solar system.
limits.generative: Unflagged generative output. In astronomy a hallucinated source is not an aesthetic defect: it is a false discovery.

how.title: How it works
how.step1Body: Time, place at whatever precision you choose, optics, filter and licence. EXIF is read in your browser and you correct whatever is wrong.
how.step2Body: Every frame is plate-solved and characterized: PSF, sky background, airmass, quality. Without that you cannot combine anything properly.
how.step3Title: You pick the frames and see the plan
how.step3Body: Before anything is queued you see which photos go in, which are blocked and why, the resulting licence and the estimated cost.

picker.title: Licence
picker.subtitle: Decide what other people can do with this photo.
picker.freezeWarning: Careful: as soon as anyone downloads this photo or it enters a published reconstruction, the licence freezes and from then on it can only be relaxed, never tightened. This is what Creative Commons themselves say: they are irrevocable for whoever already received the work.
picker.freezeLocked: This licence has been frozen since {date}: you can only change it to a more permissive one.
picker.allowAiTraining: Allow this photo to train reconstruction models
picker.allowAiTrainingHelp: Independent of the licence: Creative Commons say nothing about model training and we do not want to hide behind that ambiguity. If you withdraw it, the photo is purged from future training snapshots.
picker.allowDerivatives: Allow this photo as a frame in other people's reconstructions
picker.allowDerivativesHelp: Also independent of the licence. If you withdraw it, your photo stays published but nobody can put it in a stack.
picker.ndForcesNoStacks: You picked a no-derivatives licence: for consistency, this photo cannot be used as a frame in reconstructions. The checkbox is disabled.

CC0-1.0.name: Public domain (CC0 1.0)
CC0-1.0.description: You waive all your rights. Anyone can use the photo for anything, including commercially, without crediting you. We still credit you in ATTRIBUTION.md anyway.

CC-BY-4.0.name: Attribution (CC BY 4.0)
CC-BY-4.0.description: Anyone can use and modify it, including commercially, as long as they credit you.

CC-BY-SA-4.0.name: Attribution + ShareAlike (CC BY-SA 4.0)
CC-BY-SA-4.0.description: Like the previous one, but any derivative must carry this same licence. It is contagious: it spreads to every reconstruction your photo enters.

CC-BY-NC-4.0.name: Attribution + NonCommercial (CC BY-NC 4.0)
CC-BY-NC-4.0.description: It can be used and modified with credit, but not for commercial purposes. It is contagious: if your photo enters a reconstruction, the output is NonCommercial too.

CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.name: Attribution + NonCommercial + ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.description: No commercial use and derivatives must carry the same licence. Both conditions spread.

CC-BY-ND-4.0.name: Attribution + NoDerivatives (CC BY-ND 4.0)
CC-BY-ND-4.0.description: It can be redistributed unchanged, even commercially, but not modified. Because it forbids derivatives, your photo cannot enter any reconstruction.

CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0.name: Attribution + NonCommercial + NoDerivatives (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0.description: Unchanged, non-commercial redistribution only. Your photo cannot enter any reconstruction.

ARR.name: All rights reserved
ARR.description: Nobody may reuse it without your explicit permission. It is shown in the gallery but takes part in no reconstruction and is not downloadable.

builder.title: Reconstruction builder
builder.subtitle: Pick the frames, check the plan, and only then launch the job.
builder.empty: The builder is empty. Add photos from Explore or from an object page.
builder.pipelineHelp: Classical pipelines are deterministic and invent nothing. Ones that use a learned model are always labelled in the output.

classical-stack-v1.name: Classical stack
classical-stack-v1.description: WCS reprojection and a sum weighted by PSF and variance. Deterministic, no learned model.

drizzle-v1.name: Drizzle
drizzle-v1.description: Spreads each input pixel onto a finer grid using the sub-pixel diversity between observers. Recovers sampling, not optical resolution.

burst-sr-v1.name: Multi-frame super-resolution (learned model)
burst-sr-v1.description: Learned fusion on top of the classical stack. Always shipped labelled and with an uncertainty map.
